solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Axe literally bit by bit setter in opening or completion

parts.note: the word axe spelt letter by letter, with its middle letter written as the Greek letter it resembles, chi: A, CHI, E

indicators.note: in says the setter's pronoun sits inside the word for an opening

parts.note: a vent is an opening or outlet
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A woodsman's axe bites a tree bit by bit, from first cut to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'literally' and 'bit by bit' ask for Axe spelt out letter by letter, reading X as the Greek letter chi. 'in' signals the insertion of the setter's pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: An achievement is the accomplishing or finishing of something, a synonym for completion.

clue.text: Routine grounds for waste management contrast

parts.note: common land is unenclosed ground, traditionally called waste because nobody cultivates it
or introduces an alternative, setting one thing against another
a garden is ground that is managed and tended, the opposite of a common

explanation.surface: A council argues over which grounds to use for dumping rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The contrast is between unmanaged common land and a managed garden, joined by OR. A tentative reading: the blogger himself was unsure.
explanation.definitionFit: Common-or-garden is an idiom for ordinary or everyday, so it matches routine used as an adjective.

clue.text: Lying up having day in Bora Bora?

indicators.note: having day in means the island word holds the abbreviation for day within it

parts.note: Bora Bora is in French Polynesia, so it is an example of an île, French for island; the question mark flags the example

explanation.surface: Someone lazing about on a South Pacific holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: The island must be named in French, ÎLE, because Bora Bora is French Polynesian.
explanation.definitionFit: To be lying up is to be resting and inactive, which is what idle means.

clue.text: Nashville's old name mired in depravity and destructive force

indicators.note: mired in means stuck inside, so the old word and the name letter go within the depravity word

parts.note: vice is depravity or wickedness
ole is the folksy spelling of old in the Grand Ole Opry, Nashville's famous country music show

explanation.surface: A city's former name has become mixed up in sleaze and violent force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nashville's old name' looks like a historical name for the city; instead it is OLE (from the Grand Ole Opry) plus N.
explanation.definitionFit: Violence is physical force used to hurt or damage, the sense of destructive force.

clue.text: Couples in Mary Tudor's reign formed after adequate deliberation

indicators.note: couples are pairs, so the opening pair of letters is taken from each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Royal marriages under Queen Mary I were arranged after careful thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couples in' takes the first two letters of each word: MA, TU, RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mature judgement or plan is one reached after careful thought, as in 'on mature reflection'.

clue.text: Swede regularly entered Portugal

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word entered, here the even-placed ones

parts.note: P is the international vehicle registration letter for Portugal

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian traveller crossing the border into Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swede' looks like a Swedish person but it is the vegetable; NEEP is the Scottish word for a swede (rutabaga).
explanation.definitionFit: Neep is the Scots name for the swede or turnip, served with haggis.

clue.text: Around noon took leave of warlord carrying Aldershot's latest weapon

indicators.note: around means the farewell phrase surrounds the letter for noon

parts.note: to see someone off is to say goodbye as they leave, so saw off means took leave of

indicators.note: carrying means the warlord word holds the last letter of the town inside it

parts.note: a shogun was a Japanese military ruler or warlord

indicators.note: latest picks the final letter of the town's name

explanation.surface: At midday a soldier said goodbye to a warlord holding Aldershot's newest firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'latest' takes T, the last letter of Aldershot (a British Army garrison town), and 'carrying' puts it in SHOGUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawn-off shotgun is a firearm with a shortened barrel, so it is one kind of weapon.

clue.text: Minimum personnel on shift for instance that can provide maximum access

parts.note: a skeleton staff or crew is the smallest number of people needed to keep things running
the shift key on a keyboard is an example of a key

explanation.surface: A night shift run by a skeleton staff, someone holding the keys to everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' looks like a work period, matching 'personnel'; it is the keyboard key.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton key is a master key that opens many locks, giving the widest possible access.

clue.text: That woman taking in shops frequently gets support for lumbar region

indicators.note: taking in means the pronoun for that woman surrounds the shops and frequently words

parts.note: she is the pronoun for that woman
a mall is a group of shops
oft is an old word for often, or frequently
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: A woman who goes shopping often ends up needing a support for her aching lower back.
explanation.definitionFit: The small of the back is the narrow lower part of the back, which is the lumbar region of the spine.

clue.text: Rates for Spooner's Republican sleuths perhaps?

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: Spooner's signals the Reverend Spooner's habit of swapping sounds between two words; here the vowel sounds swap

parts.note: the Republicans are a political party, and perhaps flags the example
tecs is a slang shortening of detectives, or sleuths

explanation.surface: Asking what Spooner would make of private detectives working for the Republicans.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'Spooner's' swaps the vowel sounds, not the opening consonants, and only the second half of the answer is spoonerised. In Britain 'rates' were a local tax on property.
explanation.definitionFit: Rates were a council levy charged on the value of homes and buildings, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Chamber discharge is audible

indicators.note: is audible says the discharge word is to be heard, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: rheum is a watery discharge from the eyes or nose

explanation.surface: A shot fired in a chamber can be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber is a room, especially a private or formal one.

clue.text: Considered by judges as registered in capital

indicators.note: in says the registered letter goes inside the capital word

parts.note: capital comes from the Latin for head, and a capital sits at the head of something
R in a circle is the symbol for a registered trademark

explanation.surface: A case heard by judges in the capital city's registry.
explanation.definitionFit: A case that has been heard is one a court has listened to and judged.

clue.text: Dye best linked with the Netherlands

indicators.note: linked with means the two pairs are interlocked, their letters alternating like links of a chain

parts.note: A1 means first-class or best, written here as AI
NL is the international code for the Netherlands

explanation.surface: Top-quality dye linked with Dutch production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'linked with' interleaves A-I with N-L: A, N, I, L.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the indigo plant and the blue colouring made from it.

clue.text: Is Pele endlessly running round this pitch?

indicators.note: running round says these letters are moved about into a new order
endlessly drops the footballer's final letter

explanation.surface: Asking whether the great Brazilian footballer is forever running round this football pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts Pele to PEL; 'running round' rearranges IS + PEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiel is a sales patter or glib speech, which is what a sales pitch is.

clue.text: Lament passing of month — one with R in

indicators.note: with R in means the letter R is put inside the word for one

parts.note: 'un is a dialect form of one, as in 'a good 'un'

explanation.surface: Grieving at the end of a month containing the letter R.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is 'UN, the dialect form, as in 'a little 'un'.
explanation.definitionFit: To mourn someone is to grieve over their death, lamenting their passing.

clue.text: Potential customer's view

definitions.meaning: in sales a likely future buyer is called a ...
an extensive view of a landscape

explanation.surface: What a would-be buyer thinks of the product.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is both a possible client and a wide outlook over scenery.

clue.text: Ceiling well formed originally and in good condition

parts.note: so can mean well, as in 'so, what now?'

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of the word formed

parts.note: fit means in good physical condition

explanation.surface: A well-made ceiling still in sound condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A soffit is the underside of an arch, balcony or eave, a kind of ceiling.

clue.text: Ingenue twisted body in dance

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the dance word

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: twisted says the letters of body are wrenched into another order

explanation.surface: A naive young dancer contorting her body at a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' rearranges body to BYDO, and 'in' places that inside the dance word.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby doll is a naive, childlike young woman, which is what ingenue means.

clue.text: Bit of a good egg arguably about to be tormented

indicators.note: about turns those letters round to read the other way
bit of says the letters are found within the run good egg arguably

explanation.surface: Even a decent fellow is about to get teased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of' takes DEGGAR from 'good egg arguably', which 'about' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: To rag someone is to tease or torment them, so ragged means tormented.

clue.text: Military body rejects refusal to obey superior with taunt

indicators.note: rejects means turns back, so the refusal and taunt are read from right to left

parts.note: 'No sir!' is a refusal addressed to a superior officer
to rag is to taunt or tease

explanation.surface: An army unit spurns a soldier's insubordination and mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejects' reads the whole string backwards; 'taunt' here means rag, as in to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrison is a body of troops stationed in a town or fort.

clue.text: People employed on a Scottish island

parts.note: staff are the people employed by an organisation

explanation.surface: Workers posted to a remote Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffa is a small island in the Inner Hebrides, famous for Fingal's Cave.

clue.text: Tale that's long without slightest hint of ending

indicators.note: without means the letter that follows is removed

parts.note: to long for something is to yearn

indicators.note: slightest hint of picks the first letter of ending

explanation.surface: A story that drags on with no sign of finishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective for the tale; it is the verb YEARN, which loses E.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarn is a long, often far-fetched story.

clue.text: Foundation remains

definitions.meaning: a foundation garment is a corset
remains as a verb means stops in one place or continues

explanation.definitionFit: Stays are an old-fashioned corset, a foundation garment, and stays also means remains in place.

clue.text: Book as far as Maine

parts.note: to means as far as, as in 'up to here'
ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine

explanation.surface: A book that goes all the way to Maine.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a book, usually a large and weighty one.

clue.text: Cover for front of mobiles (but not sides) — i.e. cells

indicators.note: but not sides means the outer letters at each side are taken away

parts.note: a fascia is the detachable front cover of a mobile phone

explanation.surface: A phone case covering the front but not the sides of a mobile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not sides' strips F and A from FASCIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Asci are the sac-like cells in which some fungi form their spores.

clue.text: Draw spades to lead in pack

indicators.note: to lead means the spades letter goes in front

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in card games
to draw is to pull, or tow

explanation.surface: A card player draws spades to lead from the pack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pack' looks like a deck of cards; it is the verb, to stow away.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow is to pack things away neatly.

clue.text: After for example being CEO space in pit in return is poor bargain

indicators.note: in return means the whole string is turned back to front
after says the being CEO phrase follows the example abbreviation

parts.note: eg is short for exempli gratia, for example
a chief executive is at the top of the company

indicators.note: in puts the printer's space inside the pit

parts.note: fossa is Latin for ditch, used in English for a pit or hollow
an em is a printer's space

explanation.surface: A chief executive in a mine trades away something valuable for little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in return' reverses the whole string EGATTOPFOSSEMA. Esau's birthright story (Genesis 25) is the source of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Esau sold his birthright for a mess of pottage, so the phrase stands for a bad bargain.

clue.text: Treating as invalid approve keeping, having unhealthy complexion, at home

indicators.note: keeping means the approve word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking or approving of it
sallow describes a sickly yellowish complexion
in means at home

explanation.surface: A doctor ruling a pale patient unfit while still approving of them staying at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Disallowing a claim or goal means rejecting it as not valid.
